title: Classic French Toast with Cinnamon Sugar and Maple Syrup
summary: Thick bread is dipped quickly in a rich custard with extra yolks, fried in butter until set through, then finished with caramelised cinnamon sugar and maple syrup.
equipment: wire rack set in a baking tray

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
slices brioche or thick white bread, 2 cm thick (about 400 g), ideally a day old
caster sugar mixed with 1 tsp ground cinnamon

steps.title: Warm the oven
steps.text: Heat the oven to 100 °C (80 °C fan) with the rack and tray in it, ready to keep the first batch warm.

steps.title: Make the custard
steps.text: Whisk the eggs, yolks, milk, vanilla, cinnamon, brown sugar and salt in the shallow dish until smooth and frothy. Extra yolks make the inside rich and creamy.

steps.title: Heat the butter
steps.text: Melt a small knob of butter in the pan over low heat, then raise the heat to medium until it sizzles.

steps.title: Dip
steps.text: Turn 2 slices in the custard for about 5 seconds each side, so they are evenly wet but not soggy. Lift them out, let the excess drip off and lay them in the pan. Repeat to fill the pan.

steps.title: Cook through
steps.text: Fry for 2-3 minutes until golden underneath. Add a little more butter, swirl the pan, flip and cook for 2-3 minutes more over medium-low heat, until the second side is golden and the centre springs back when pressed (71 °C). If a dent stays, cook a little longer; the egg in the middle must set.

steps.title: Caramelise
steps.text: Sprinkle the tops with cinnamon sugar, flip for 20 seconds to caramelise, then sprinkle the other side.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Keep each batch warm in the oven while you cook the rest. Serve 2 slices each with the maple syrup.

tips: Soaking the bread too long is the commonest mistake; it turns soggy and won't cook through.
Slightly stale bread holds its shape best.
Keep the heat moderate so the outside doesn't burn before the middle sets.
Add fresh butter before flipping so the second side browns evenly.
storage: Best eaten straight away. Cooled slices can be refrigerated for up to 2 days or frozen for up to 1 month; reheat in a 180 °C oven or toaster until piping hot. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
